sources.title: Write-Ahead Logging
sources.why: Canonical checkpoint rules: auto-checkpoint at 1000 pages on COMMIT or last-connection close, PASSIVE only, WAL reused not truncated, starvation and reader gaps (s6), plus s11 WAL-reset bug (3.7.0-3.51.2; fixed 3.51.3, backports 3.44.6/3.50.7). Internal disagreements to validate: s3.2 names three subtypes (no TRUNCATE) and s6 says RESTART/TRUNCATE may block readers. s11.2 links Phil Eaton's no-test-hook reproducer at theconsensus.dev (403 to WebFetch here, so not listed).

sources.title: sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2() - Checkpoint a database
sources.why: Exact semantics of PASSIVE/FULL/RESTART/TRUNCATE/NOOP: busy-handler use, checkpoint lock giving SQLITE_BUSY without busy handler, fall-back to PASSIVE when the handler gives up, pnLog/pnCkpt outputs. States FULL/RESTART/TRUNCATE block writers but not readers, which differs from wal.html s6.

sources.title: PRAGMA statements (wal_checkpoint, wal_autocheckpoint, journal_size_limit, synchronous)
sources.why: Pragma-level behaviour: 3-column wal_checkpoint result (busy flag, WAL frames, checkpointed frames; -1 when not WAL), wal_autocheckpoint default 1000 with <=0 disabling and always PASSIVE, journal_size_limit default -1 so WAL is not truncated after a checkpoint, synchronous=NORMAL syncing only around checkpoints. Page is ~100 KB; fetch offset 100000 for the tail.

sources.title: sqlite3_wal_hook() - Write-Ahead Log Commit Hook
sources.why: How custom checkpoint policies are wired: callback runs after COMMIT with the WAL page count and may itself checkpoint; registering a hook replaces the default autocheckpoint (and the autocheckpoint pragma overwrites a hook); the application must then checkpoint periodically or the WAL grows without bound.

sources.title: WAL-mode File Format
sources.why: Internals the user docs omit: nBackfill vs mxFrame, five read marks and WAL_READ_LOCK(N) promises that cap how far a checkpoint may backfill, exclusive WAL_CKPT_LOCK, WAL reset only when nBackfill equals mxFrame with no locks on read locks 1-4, and clean close checkpointing then unlinking the -wal and -shm files.

sources.title: Wal2 mode (SQLite wal2 branch documentation)
sources.why: Maintainers acknowledge standard WAL 'may grow indefinitely if the checkpointer never gets a chance to finish' and document the two-file wal2 design that bounds it. Scopes the fix: wal2 databases open only with SQLite built from the branch (SQLITE_NOTADB otherwise), no direct wal-to-wal2 switch, wal-hook still runs inside COMMIT.

sources.title: src/wal.c (SQLite source, master branch)
sources.why: Ground truth for walCheckpoint(): mxSafeFrame derived from the read-mark locks, busy handler suppressed for PASSIVE (asserted), TRUNCATE path via walRestartHdr plus sqlite3OsTruncate to 0, caller must hold the checkpoint lock. File is ~184 KB; sqlite3WalCheckpoint() lies past char 100000, so fetch with offsets.

sources.title: When do readers actually stop using the WAL? Is there a contradiction? (SQLite User Forum, 2024-02-01)
sources.why: Dan Kennedy (SQLite developer) explains readers fix their end mark when the read transaction opens, so a PASSIVE checkpoint copies frames but leaves them in the WAL and only a completed RESTART/TRUNCATE lets the log be reused; resolves an apparent contradiction in the docs and shows starvation from the reader side.

sources.title: How Tailscale helped find the SQLite WAL-Reset bug
sources.why: Production postmortem (Alex Chan, 2026-08-12): 19 corruptions in six months from a checkpoint-vs-write race; Tailscale's manual, aggressive checkpointing raised its exposure; covers the tmstmpvfs diagnosis, the withdrawn 3.52.0, and the 3.51.3/3.53.0 fix path. Scopes both 'WAL is corruption-safe' and 'the bug is too rare to matter'.

sources.title: Breaking the WAL (reproducing the SQLite WAL-reset bug)
sources.why: Independent reproduction (Carl Sverre, 2026-08-12): a generic concurrent write-plus-checkpoint workload with integrity-check assertions hit the bug in about 15 minutes on 3.51.2 and ran clean on 3.51.3; tests the SQLite team's statement that it needed special test code to trigger it.

sources.title: WAL Truncate Threshold Configuration
sources.why: Three-tier external checkpoint policy with defaults (min-checkpoint-page-count 1000 PASSIVE, checkpoint-interval 1m PASSIVE, truncate-page-n 121359 ~500 MB blocking TRUNCATE as last resort) and its cost: a forced TRUNCATE waits for readers, blocks writes, and shows up as 'database is locked'.

sources.title: Tips & Caveats
sources.why: Replication tools hold a read lock to stop other processes checkpointing; an application checkpoint between Litestream's own forces a fresh full snapshot; recommends PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint = 0 in the app plus busy_timeout.

sources.title: Taking control of the SQLite WAL (rqlite)
sources.why: Replicated-database design (2026-05-12): automatic checkpoint off, user checkpoint pragmas blocked, TRUNCATE checkpoint per Raft snapshot with a 250 ms default busy wait; handles partial, and checkpointed-but-not-truncated, outcomes using WAL header salts.

sources.title: Something you probably want to know about if you're using SQLite in Golang
sources.why: Reproduced failure (Piotr Jastrzebski, 2023-08-03): an unclosed database/sql rows keeps a read open, WAL reached 42 MB beside a 4 kB database, and manual wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) did not shrink it; shows diagnosing by comparing file sizes.

sources.title: How to VACUUM SQLite in WAL Mode (and why you need a checkpoint)
sources.why: Shows a PASSIVE auto-checkpoint after VACUUM leaves the WAL at full size (VACUUM writes the rebuilt database into the WAL as one transaction) and only wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) reclaims it; links a better-sqlite3 test harness (2025-11-02).

sources.title: Checkpoint starvation - Issue #10559 - syncthing/syncthing
sources.why: Live, still-open starvation case (opened 2026-02-04): reporter argues many short overlapping reads leave no gap for a maintenance TRUNCATE and that SQLite's own PASSIVE auto-checkpoint makes manual checkpoints fail; maintainer calmh disputes the analysis (2026-09-12), so treat the causal claims as unproven.

angles: What a checkpoint is: copying committed WAL frames into the main database file (mxFrame, nBackfill, read marks, reader end marks) and why that differs from resetting or truncating the WAL

Automatic checkpoint triggers and defaults: 1000 pages on COMMIT by the committing connection, last-connection close, SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT, wal_autocheckpoint pragma, sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint versus sqlite3_wal_hook replacement; automatic checkpoints are always PASSIVE

Checkpoint modes PASSIVE/FULL/RESTART/TRUNCATE/NOOP: locks taken, busy-handler behaviour, SQLITE_BUSY fall-back to PASSIVE, who is blocked (writers versus readers), pragma 3-column result versus C output parameters

WAL file size lifecycle: reuse after checkpoint, WAL reset conditions, truncation only via TRUNCATE or journal_size_limit, last-connection cleanup and SQLITE_FCNTL_PERSIST_WAL, large write transactions and VACUUM inflating the WAL

Checkpoint starvation and other reasons a WAL does not shrink: long or overlapping readers, unfinalized statements or unclosed Go rows, an application checkpointer colliding with auto-checkpoint, reader gaps; diagnosis via the wal_checkpoint busy flag and frame counts
Performance and durability trade-offs: read slowdown as the WAL grows, checkpoint sync cost, synchronous=NORMAL syncing only around checkpoints, writer stalls from blocking modes

Application-run and replication-driven checkpoint policies: idle-time or background checkpointers, Litestream thresholds and read lock, rqlite snapshot-driven TRUNCATE, Syncthing pool-release heuristic

WAL-reset bug: trigger conditions, affected range 3.7.0-3.51.2, fix and backport versions, withdrawn 3.52.0, exposure with manual aggressive checkpointing, disputed rarity (SQLite 'unlikely' versus Antithesis reproduction and Phil Eaton's reproducer)
Alternatives and version scope: wal2 branch and BEGIN CONCURRENT, and which released SQLite versions carry which checkpoint-related fixes

Documentation inconsistencies to validate: wal.html lists three subtypes and says RESTART/TRUNCATE may block readers, while c3ref/wal_checkpoint_v2 lists five modes including NOOP and says writers, not readers, are blocked
